arxiv-1406-7210.title: Asymptotic Stability and Decay Rates of Homogeneous Positive Systems With Bounded and Unbounded Delays
arxiv-1406-7210.creator: Hamid Reza Feyzmahdavian, Themistoklis Charalambous, Mikael Johansson
arxiv-1406-7210.description: A 2014 arXiv research paper by Hamid Reza Feyzmahdavian, Themistoklis Charalambous, Mikael Johansson. There are several results on the stability of nonlinear positive systems in the presence of time delays. However, most of them assume that the delays are constant. This paper considers time-varying , possibly unbounded, delays and establishes asymptotic stability and bounds the decay rate of a significant class of nonlinear positive systems which includes positive linear systems as a special case.

arxiv-2112-12628.title: Transition between growth of dense and porous films: Theory of dual-layer SEI
arxiv-2112-12628.creator: Lars von Kolzenberg, Martin Werres =, Jonas Tetzloff, Birger Horstmann
arxiv-2112-12628.description: Abstract The formation of passivating films is a common aging phenomenon, for example in weathering of rocks, silicon, and metals. In many cases, a dual-layer structure with a dense inner and a porous outer layer emerges. However, the origin of this dual-layer growth is so far not fully understood.

arxiv-2208-10909.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Misha Chernobai, Tim Shilkin. In this paper we prove the existence, uniqueness and regularity of weak solutions to the Dirichlet problem for an elliptic equation with a drift b b satisfying div b ≤ 0 \mathop{\rm div}b\leq 0 in Ω \Omega .

arxiv-2308-07827.title: Learning Better Keypoints for Multi-Object 6DoF Pose Estimation
arxiv-2308-07827.creator: Yangzheng Wu, Michael Greenspan
arxiv-2308-07827.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yangzheng Wu, Michael Greenspan. We address the problem of keypoint selection, and find that the performance of 6DoF pose estimation methods can be improved when pre-defined keypoint locations are learned, rather than being heuristically selected as has been the standard approach. We found that accuracy and efficiency can be improved by training a graph network to select a set of disperse keypoints with similarly distributed votes.

arxiv-2309-01983.title: Quaternary Conjucyclic Codes with an Application to EAQEC Codes
arxiv-2309-01983.creator: Md Ajaharul Hossain, Ramakrishna Bandi
arxiv-2309-01983.description: Abstract Conjucyclic codes are part of a family of codes that includes cyclic, constacyclic, and quasi-cyclic codes, among others. Despite their importance in quantum error correction, they have not received much attention in the literature. This paper focuses on additive conjucyclic (ACC) codes over 𝔽 4 \mathbb{F}_{4} and investigates their properties.

arxiv-2312-07875.title: Enhance Sketch Recognition’s Explainability via Semantic Component-Level Parsing
arxiv-2312-07875.creator: Guangming Zhu, Siyuan Wang, Tianci Wu, Liang Zhang
arxiv-2312-07875.description: Abstract Free-hand sketches are appealing for humans as a universal tool to depict the visual world. Humans can recognize varied sketches of a category easily by identifying the concurrence and layout of the intrinsic semantic components of the category, since humans draw free-hand sketches based a common consensus that which types of semantic components constitute each sketch category.

arxiv-2410-02271.title: CoLLAP: Co ntrastive L ong-form L anguage- A udio P retraining with Musical Temporal Structure Augmentation
arxiv-2410-02271.creator: Junda Wu, Warren Li, Zachary Novack, Amit Namburi, Carol Chen, Julian McAuley
arxiv-2410-02271.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Junda Wu, Warren Li, Zachary Novack, Amit Namburi, Carol Chen, Julian McAuley. Modeling temporal characteristics plays a significant role in the representation learning of audio waveform. We propose Co ntrastive L ong-form L anguage- A udio P retraining ( CoLLAP ) to significantly extend the perception window for both the input audio (up to 5 minutes) and the language descriptions (exceeding 250 words), while enabling contrastive learning across modalities and temporal dynamics.

arxiv-2503-21790.title: March Madness Tournament Predictions Model: A Mathematical Modeling Approach
arxiv-2503-21790.creator: Christian McIver cmciver@college.harvard.edu, Karla Avalos karlaavalos@college.harvard.edu, Nikhil Nayak nnayak@g.harvard.edu
arxiv-2503-21790.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Christian McIver cmciver@college.harvard.edu, Karla Avalos karlaavalos@college.harvard.edu, Nikhil Nayak nnayak@g.harvard.edu. This paper proposes a model to predict the outcome of the March Madness tournament based on historical NCAA basketball data since 2013. The framework of this project is a simplification of the FiveThrityEight NCAA March Madness prediction model, where the only four predictors of interest are Adjusted Offensive Efficiency (ADJOE), Adjusted Defensive Efficiency (ADJDE), Power Rating, and Two-Point Shooting Percentage Allowed.

pmc-11497262.title: Predictive value of the dynamic systemic immune-inflammation index in the prognosis of patients with intracerebral hemorrhage: a 10-year retrospective analysis
pmc-11497262.creator: Wenchao Ma, Xiaoming Wu, Lang Yang, Yumin Yang, Hao Zhang, Yan Wang, Haiying Xue, Xiaodong Long
pmc-11497262.description: Background and purposeThe systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) is a novel immune inflammatory marker which has been proven to have excellent predictive value for many diseases. pmc-11629197.title: Injectable hyaluronate-L- cysteine gel potentiates photothermal therapy in osteosarcoma via vorinostat-copper cell death
pmc-11629197.creator: Sizhen Wang, Hanzhe Zhang, Tianheng Chen, Weiwei Jiang, Feng Wang, Yuhao Yu, Beibei Guo, Jia Xu, Feng Yang, Qinglin Kang, Zhiqiang Ma
pmc-11629197.description: The prognosis for osteosarcoma patients, a devastating malignancy affecting young individuals, remains grim despite multimodal therapeutic advances. Recently, the advent of cuproptosis, a novel programmed cell death, offers hope in fighting osteosarcoma. In this study, we introduce SAHAm@{[Cu(HA-Cys)2]Cl2}n, an injectable hyaluronate-L-cysteine hydrogel that integrates both copper ions (Cu2+) and vorinostat (SAHA) for the possible therapeutic effect.

pmc-11749039.title: Orthodontic Treatment of Anterior Open Bite Caused by a Car Accident

pmc-11749039.description: This article outlines the orthodontic treatment of a 21-year-old female patient with an open bite and temporomandibular joint disorders (TMDs) that developed after a severe car accident. The treatment plan utilized temporary anchorage devices (TADs) for upper molar intrusion to correct the open bite without resorting to orthognathic surgery.

pmc-12504994.title: Sumac (Rhus coriaria L.) Supplementation on High-Sensitivity C-Reactive Protein Concentrations in Adults: A Systematic Review and Dose-Response Meta-Analysis
pmc-12504994.creator: Mostafa Shahraki Jazinaki, Hossein Bahari, Iman Rahnama, Mohammad Safarian, Mahsa Malekahmadi
pmc-12504994.description: BackgroundChronic low-grade inflammation is implicated in the development of various metabolic and cardiovascular disorders. Sumac (Rhus coriaria L.) is a medicinal plant with potential anti-inflammatory properties. However, the effects of sumac supplementation on inflammatory biomarkers, particularly high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), remain controversial.ObjectivesThis systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effect of sumac supplementation on hs-CRP concentrations in adults.

pmc-12688432.creator: Mitsuhiko Shoda, Mitsuru Takami, Kimitake Imamura, Ken-ichi Tani, Hidehiro Iwai, Yusuke Nakanishi, Atsushi Murakami, Shogo Yonehara, Hiroyuki Asada, Takahiro Kunigita, Mari Yamamoto, Ryosuke Takahashi, Koji Fukuzawa, Hiromasa Otake
pmc-12688432.description: BackgroundAtrial functional mitral regurgitation (FMR) results from left atrial enlargement and dysfunction, typically observed in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). uslaw-usc-t28-s2109.title: 28 U.S.C. § 2109 — Quorum of Supreme Court justices absent
uslaw-usc-t28-s2109.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t28-s2109.description: United States Code, Title 28 (Judiciary And Judicial Procedure); Part V (Procedure); Chapter 133 (Review—Miscellaneous Provisions). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. If a case brought to the Supreme Court by direct appeal from a district court cannot be heard and determined because of the absence of a quorum of qualified justices, the Chief Justice of the United States may order it remitted.
